$comment: Every line the GitHub Copilot CLI course says (docs/voices.md). This course is text only (course.json → "voice": false): each line is a caption that holds for its reading time, and a press moves it on. `tools/voice/generate.ts --course copilot-cli` writes the captions into public/voice/ (no speech service).

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Welcome aboard, Captain! I’m Juno, your first mate.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Each island teaches a chapter of the GitHub Copilot CLI for Beginners course. Finish its quests to earn its Seal.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Quests fill your Logbook and your purse. Then we sail on!

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: And look out for starfish. They hide on every island.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Now, open the chest, Captain. Our chart’s inside.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Ahoy, Captain! Up here! I’m Wingman, your parrot and first mate.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Every island out here teaches a chapter of the GitHub Copilot CLI for Beginners course, and each one has a Seal to earn.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: We’re on Anchorage Cay, where you’ll install Copilot CLI, sign in, and check it works. Nell’s by the harbourmaster’s door, so start with her.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Your tasks are in the top left, and the compass up top points to the next one.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: And seven starfish are hidden around Anchorage Cay. Your count’s in the top right.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Stuck? Press Q for a hint. I’ll ride on your shoulder. Hints are my job. Decisions are yours!

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Welcome back, Captain! Your next task’s in the top left.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Morning, Captain! To sail from Anchorage, you need papers: a GitHub account with Copilot access.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: You’ll want terminal basics too, commands like cd and ls. The list’s in my chest.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Not sure you’ve got access? Check your status at github.com/settings/copilot. You should see Copilot Individual, Business, Enterprise, or GitHub Education.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Papers in order! Ezra’s at his chart table by the pier. He’ll get the course aboard.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Papers in order. Off you go!

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: A sealed captain! Fair winds.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: Get your papers from Nell first, Captain. Then we’ll talk charts.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: Every captain needs the course aboard, its sample book app and all. There are two ways to get it.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: Don’t want to install anything? Fork the repository and make a GitHub Codespace. Copilot CLI’s ready to go there, with Python and pytest. You’ll just need to sign in.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: On your own machine? Clone the repository to get the course samples, then cd into copilot-cli-for-beginners.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: Course aboard. Bo’s at his gear rack beside me. He’ll get Copilot CLI installed.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Bo Marlin, quartermaster. Let’s get GitHub Copilot CLI installed. Pick the way that fits your system.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Got Node.js? Then npm’s a quick way. On macOS or Linux, there’s Homebrew or the install script. On Windows, WinGet.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: In a Codespace, you can skip this. The CLI’s already there.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: That’s the CLI aboard. Pim and Pol are at the end of the pier. They’ll get you signed in.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: I’m Pim, and that’s Pol. Once Copilot CLI’s installed, we’ll get you signed in. Bo’s by the pier foot.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Not yet, Captain. Install the CLI with Bo first.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Open a terminal at the root of the copilot-cli-for-beginners repository, and start the CLI. Just type copilot.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: First, it asks you to trust the folder. You can trust it one time, or across all future sessions.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Then sign in with your GitHub account. Type /login, and pick Sign in with your browser.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: No browser? On a remote or headless terminal, like SSH, you get a one-time code instead. That’s the device code flow.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Visit github.com/login/device on another machine, and enter the code to finish.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: And it sticks. You only sign in again if your token expires, or you sign out.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Signed in and trusted. Juno’s by your ship, Captain. Time for your first words.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Token expired one day? Just run /login again.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Juno, your first mate. You’re installed and signed in, so let’s check it works.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: At Copilot CLI’s prompt, you ask in plain words. Try this one: Say hello and tell me what you can help with.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Two fittings on the rail behind me. The brass speaking tube goes to Copilot’s prompt. The iron hatch goes down to the shell. Your call, Captain.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: It’s a request for Copilot, not a shell command. Pick the fitting on the rail that carries it.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: That went down to the shell, Captain. The shell runs commands like cd and ls. Requests go to Copilot’s prompt.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: The shell runs commands, Captain. Ask Copilot through its prompt: the speaking tube.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Hear that? A friendly answer, listing what Copilot CLI can help with.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Yours will be worded differently. Your model, tools, and responses will differ.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Then try it on the course’s book app. An @ in front of a file’s path brings that file in.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: When you’re done, /exit leaves the CLI. Nell’s waiting by your bow with the Harbormaster’s Trial.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: The crew’s heard your first words. Nell’s waiting by your bow with the Harbormaster’s Trial.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: The crew’s proud of you, Captain. Wherever you sail next, they’re listening.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: You’re set up, Captain. Before your ship gets her name, there’s the Harbormaster’s Trial: seven questions on what you’ve done.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Seven questions, Captain. No answers from me in there, only nudges.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: The Seal of Anchorage, and well earned. Now, about that ship.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: No ship leaves Anchorage without a name, Captain, and yours has been waiting all morning.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Fair winds to her, and to all who sail in her!

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: She suits you, Captain. Fair winds.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Crew’s aboard, Captain.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Right, a quick sailing lesson. The gangway’s down now, so walk up it to take the helm. W and S trim the sails, and A and D steer.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: The compass up top points back to the pier. Bring her alongside and press E, and I’ll help you dock.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: The other islands aren’t charted in this course yet, Captain. Until they are, these waters are yours.
